_comment: Macedonian month names are the international Latin-derived set, like Bulgarian, Serbian and Russian and UNLIKE Czech (leden), Croatian (siječanj), Polish (styczeń) and Ukrainian (січень), which kept the Slavic nature-names. Macedonian HAS a native set too — коложег, сечко, цутар, тревен, косар, жетвар, златец, житар, гроздобер, листопад, студен, снежник — but it is archaic and literary and never appears on a document, so it is deliberately not used here. They are written LOWERCASE. monthsInDate is IDENTICAL to months, and that identity is grammar rather than a shortcut: Macedonian has no noun cases at all, so there is no genitive for a date to switch into — 16 август 2026 carries the same form as the bare month name, where Czech would write 16. srpna. Weekdays are Sunday-first per the field contract, but the Macedonian week starts on MONDAY, and the names prove it: среда is "the middle" and четврток and петок are literally "fourth" and "fifth" counted from понеделник. Note the spellings against Bulgarian — среда not сряда, четврток not четвъртък, петок not петък. Unlike Bulgarian, a Macedonian date takes no closing " г." abbreviation; the year stands bare.
